title: Impact Microscope — manager sparring notebook
content:
Purpose: a compact, evidence-first prep guide to run 1:1 sparring with my manager. Use the microscope approach: focus on 1 concrete impact claim, the clearest evidence that supports it, a short risk note, and the exact ask. Keep everything rehearseable in 90 seconds.

How to use this doc (quick):
- Before sync: pick one claim to surface. Update the top-line metric and one supporting artifact.
- During sync: deliver the 90s pitch, pause for manager reaction, then bring the ask or decision needed.
- After sync: capture commitments and next-check date.

Current prioritized claim (Q1–Q2):
- Claim: Enabled a 17% reduction in average token spend for hosted-api customers on text-generation routes by shipping two batching+cache heuristics and a model profile guide.
- Why it matters: immediate monthly cost saving for customers, lower unit cost for Redwood, helps justify priority for Optimize productization.
- Key metric (signal): avg tokens per completed request (text-gen-prod-v2) dropped from 312 -> 258 (17.3%) across top 15 customers (rolling 14d).
- Supporting artifact: experiment dashboard (EXPT-2319) and rollout notes (PR #489).
- Quick evidence snippet to read out: "We measured token-per-response at the routing layer; after enabling prefix-KV cache and adaptive batch window for bursty queues, median latency increased <5ms while tokens/request fell 17% for the top cohort."

Risk and counterfactuals (short):
- Risk: some edge-case prompts saw hallucination regressions when truncation heuristics were applied; isolated to 2 customers.
- Mitigation: rollback flag + targeted eval suite added; working on a prompt-preserving fallback.
- Ask for manager: greenlight a controlled Dedicated forensics run (2 days of infra + SRE support) to reproduce edge cases end-to-end and approve a customer outreach brief if needed.

Manager pitch (90s script):
- Opening line (10s): "Quick update: last month we shipped two runtime heuristics that lowered tokens/request by ~17% for our highest-volume text-gen routes — saves on unit cost and improves throughput economics."
- Evidence (30s): "Dashboard EXPT-2319 shows tokens/request down from 312 to 258 across top 15 accounts; latency impact minimal. We verified generation quality on our smoke prompt set but found 2 customer-specific prompt families that regressed under aggressive truncation."
- Implication + ask (20s): "I recommend a 48-hour forensics run on Dedicated with SRE and a customer outreach template ready. Approval to schedule? If yes, I'll own runbook and comms."
- Close (10s): pause for reaction, capture decision and next-step owner.

Micro-followups I will commit to if approved:
- Prep runbook + minimal infra checklist (by end of week).
- Draft short customer-facing note that explains: what happened, how we detect, what to expect (by EOD next Tue).
- Postmortem + adjusted eval harness to catch the prompt families (owner: me, due +2 weeks).

Secondary claims I may surface in the same meeting (if time):
- Claim B: Rolled out a new onboarding checklist that cut setup time for Dedicated customers from 3.2 days -> 1.9 days for initial model pinning. Evidence: onboarding survey N=12.
- Ask B: permission to include the shortened checklist as a part of the Partner onboarding playbook and a 1-hour training slot for Solutions Eng.

Rehearsal Q&A — short prompts and my candidate responses:
- Q: "How do we know this isn't just cohort drift?"
  A: "We controlled for cohort by comparing identical customer traffic windows and ran A/B across the routing policy; see EXPT-2319 notes for the control group details."
- Q: "What's the business upside?"
  A: "Lower RU cost (improved gross margin on hosted API), smaller infra footprint, and a stronger case to productize into Optimize — we estimate $75k ARR improvement if adopted by top 10 customers."
- Q: "Do we need legal or compliance involved?"
  A: "Only if customers require audit-level detail; initial outreach is informational. I'll loop Legal only if customers ask for logs or model-exact transcripts."

Personal micro-goals for next manager sync (2 weeks):
- Ship the forensics run (or share schedule).
- Deliver the customer outreach draft for review.
- Add 15 targeted prompts to the eval harness and show regression delta <1% on quality metric.

Quick todo list (next 7 days):
- [ ] Draft runbook and infra ops checklist (Nico).
- [ ] Draft customer outreach + optional FAQ (collab: Amelie).
- [ ] Schedule 2-hour forensics window with SRE (tentative: Thurs).
- [ ] Add targeted prompts to eval harness and run smoke (Jordan to help).

Notes to self (raw, short):
- Keep the pitch tight — manager likes crisp asks with proposed owners and timelines.
- Bring the control group chart toy (visual) if time: shows control vs. treatment over 14 days.
- Avoid deep technical kernel talk unless they ask; focus on customer impact and mitigations.

End checkpoint: after sync, paste manager decision here and set calendar reminder for follow-ups.

Recent manager decisions (clipboard):
- 2026-02-10: OK'd limited rollout to Dedicated forensics run (owner: Nico).
- 2026-02-18: Ask for customer comms draft before running forensics — action item added above.

Revision history (top):
- 2025-11-18: created initial template and claim.
- 2026-01-22: updated metrics from EXPT-2319 and added Risk section.
- 2026-03-01: added manager decisions and clarifying rehearsal Q&A.
